To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we verified a gate-level implementation of a 12000-gate circuit against an implementation-independent 12000-line specification using theorem proving and model checking and that we found eight previously unknown bugs in the implementation.

we verified a large, complex, gate-level circuit against an implementation-independent, high-level specification, using theorem proving to derive 56 runs of a model-checking tool, and that we discovered eight new bugs in the IM.

(a) we verified the IM against a specification of the IA-32 instruction-length detection algorithm; (b) we discovered eight previously unknown errors; (c) the errors were all in the same area; (d) the errors are all related to the same cause; and (e) the errors are related to an error in the original design specification.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the application of formal methods to the verification of hardware designs, and in particular, to the verification of industrial designs in an industrial environment.
the application of formal methods to large-scale industrial designs.
developing techniques that can be used to formally verify the correctness of complex, real-world systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our model is correct, and that the implementation of the IM meets its specification.
our verification is complete, correct, and correct.
the IM is functionally correct, and that it has been formally verified to be so.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the verification took 1.3 person-years and that the bugs were detected by a combination of model-checking runs (which took 1.1 person-years) and theorem proving (which took 0.2 person-year).
we have verified a gate-level design against a high-level specification.
we were able to verify a very complex circuit in a reasonable amount of time and that the verification found several bugs that were not detected in previous testing.
The main takeaway from our work is that
theorem proving can be used to verify large circuits, and that theorem provers can be used in industrial verification environments.
theorem proving can be used to discover bugs in complex industrial designs and that theorem proving can work well with model checking. We
theorem proving can be applied successfully to industrial problems.
